courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So we added the geolocation, the possibility for users to auto-locate themselves and it's working quite
nice and we also saw that it works on mobile devices, which is of course the core idea behind this, we tap
into real native API features
and that's something I really want to highlight because it is important to understand and get right.
Here when we're locating ourselves, in the browser,
we use a browser API,
the geolocation API is provided in the browser too. When we're doing this on the native devices here,
we really tap into native device features,
so under the hood, we use the Capacitor bridge
I was referring to earlier in this module on the slides.
So this is now not using a browser feature here but really a native device feature
and this will become even clearer once we add the camera or once we try to access the camera.
So for that, let's dive into a new core plugin and that would be the camera plugin Capacitor offers
us. Now for that
camera plugin, to use it,
we first of all have to make sure that we again have all these permissions set up. So let's dive into
the Android folder and there in the Android manifest
and as we can see we should have these three permissions set.
Now if we have a look here, we have these external storage permissions
and regarding the camera, we have that permission down there,
so nothing needs to be changed on Android. On iOS,
if we go into the app app folder and then the info.plist, there we should set that
NSCameraUsageDescription key and if we have a look at the info.plist file, we have it here.
So you can customize that message again
but other than that, nothing needs to be changed here.
Now in our app, we need to change a lot though because right now, we have no component that would allow
us to pick an image,
so it's time to create a new one.
Let's say I use the Ionic CLI for that and run ionic generate components and then I want to create
that in my shared folder, just as I created that location picker, I'll create shared pickers
and now that will be my image picker,
so sitting next to that location picker component will be that image picker component
and therefore now if we reload this here, we see that image picker file.
Now how should that image picker work and look like?
Well it's pretty similar to our location picker,
I want to have a wrapping div,
I eventually want to show a preview,
I want to have a button, so I'll copy the code from there and move it in here
and yes of course therefore you could think about refactoring this into a shared component if you wanted
to.
Now I should not really need a spinner here, so let's get rid of that.
The image is definitely something I need though because I want to show a preview image,
I'll not check for any loading state though but I will check and I will use a selected image which
eventually will be set as soon as we did choose an image
and here of course, I will trigger not onPickLocation but onPickImage
and of course, the selected image property and the onPickImage method here have to be added to this
component.
The class here will also just be image, makes more sense, the location image and other than that, we're
almost fine. For that
icon on the button however, I will use the camera icon instead of the map icon which should look nicer
and for the text of course, I'll use take picture.
OK.
So these are the first steps,
now let's move on to the Typescript file and let's add that selected image property which should be
a string here, which we're referring to in our template
and of course, let's add the onPickImage method,
so here I'll add onPickImage. Now onPickImage should open the device camera and should utilize the
device camera
but I also want to provide a fallback for cases where we don't have a camera, let's say a browser or
a PC without a webcam or anything like that.
There you don't have a camera and therefore, you want to provide some fallback.
